extracted.intended_audience: people preparing and distributing press releases (PR professionals, communications staff, small businesses)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting an effective, distribution-ready press release that attracts journalists, the public, and target stakeholders. Covers headline, lead, body, assets, boilerplate, and distribution-friendly mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness and audience targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Have something to say that is of interest and target appropriate key audiences (journalists, the general public, consumers, decision-makers, influencers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is not to write for the masses but to reach relevant audiences; keeping audience in mind makes your news more engaging, readable, and more likely to be reported on, followed, and shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling headline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Google and search, include keywords in the first 60 characters. A strong headline grabs attention and helps SEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong lead paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Get to the point in the first paragraph and pique readers' interest so they'll keep reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead should convey the core news quickly and entice the reader to continue to the main body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the story and relevance in the main body
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your news engaging by focusing on the story and what’s of interest; cite facts and be authentic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep fluff to a minimum; avoid stock phrases such as “We’re proud to announce…” or “We’re pleased to…” which add little value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bullet points for dense factual information
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’re citing lots of facts or numbers, consider using bullet points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bullet points improve readability and help journalists and readers scan key facts quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include authoritative quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quotes of your organization’s CEO or experts to create personal engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists use quotes; they add a human voice and context. Ensure quotes add insight rather than generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended length
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to keep your news release between 400 and 700 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A longer press release doesn’t create greater interest — provide better information, not just more of it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual assets and branding
rubrics_metrics.description: Add video, images, and at minimum include a logo to create a visually compelling release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain text-only press releases can lose reader interest. Visuals increase engagement and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links and additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include links to your website or to additional information in case the reader wants to know more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links help keep the release short while directing readers to fuller resources; they also support SEO and traffic back to your site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social sharing functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Include social media sharing functions in your news release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for readers and journalists to share; platforms (like EIN Presswire) often provide share buttons or chicklets to simplify distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a short boilerplate (about the organization) at the bottom of the release and always include contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boilerplate can be short or provided as a link to your website. Contact details are essential so journalists can follow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and re-read your news release for grammar and spelling and always ask someone else to proof it before distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors can force corrections after distribution; external review reduces mistakes and increases professionalism.
